text:
jamie: Heads-up — ran the apples-to-apples comparison between replay harness and synthetic long-context generator. seeing a consistent ~18% p95 regression on the replay runs when kernel A is picked vs kernel B. details below.
li: oh interesting. same model/version?
jamie: yup, v2.3.1 quantized fp16 path. pinned everything except the input stream (replay vs synthetic). batch / scheduling config identical.
mateo: quick q — is it prefill-dominant traces only or mix?
jamie: mostly prefill-first traces (80% of tokens are prefill). sequence lengths skewed: mean 6k, median 4k, tail ~24k. synthetic generator matched that seqlen distribution.
sofia: do you have profiler output? kernel switch reason?
jamie: attached snippets in-thread: profiler shows different kernel selection at step boundary after prefill. replay trace ends up with more short-chunk prefill bursts which prevent continuous large-kernel runs, so we pay kernel-switch overhead and less kernel-fused work.
jamie: ```
# simplified perf trace for a single request (replay)
[0.000s] prefill chunk 0: kernel A init 12.3ms
[0.012s] prefill chunk 1: kernel A run 10.4ms
[0.022s] kv cache restore 1.1ms
[0.023s] kernel fallback -> kernel B 5.6ms (reinit)
[0.028s] decode step 0: kernel B run 2.2ms
```
li: hmm reinit costs are visible. what about batching heuristics? could replay ordering reduce batching efficiency?
jamie: yes — replay harness preserves original request interleaving, resulting in more fragmented batches (smaller effective batch size). synthetic traffic was windowed to align bursts and got 30% larger avg batch sizes.
ome: can we force batching thresholds to prioritize throughput in replay runs? i.e., increase batch wait ms for prefill-heavy flows.
sofia: we tried +5ms in a quick run — p95 improved but p50 moved up and some latency SLOs broke. tradeoff is expected.
perf-bot: automated profile summary: replay-run-1830567890 - p50 37ms, p95 198ms, avg batch size 4.1, kernel-switch events 23/1k reqs. synthetic-run-1830567900 - p50 34ms, p95 167ms, avg batch size 5.3, kernel-switch events 8/1k reqs.
omar: can we decode why kernel selection differs? maybe seqlen prediction or tokenization differences?
jamie: looked into kernel-selection logs. switching predicate uses sequence remainder and kv-cache-hit heuristics. replay traces have slightly different tokenization boundaries (chat messages with emojis and inline code) so remainder signals trigger smaller-kernel path.
li: two possible fixes: 1) make kernel-selection hysteresis (avoid switching for short-lived remainder changes) 2) post-replay normalize chunk boundaries during harness replay to match synthetic chunking for apples-to-apples comparison.
mateo: i'd prefer (2) for benchmarking to get stable apples-to-apples numbers, and (1) for product to reduce regressive behavior in production.
sofia: agreed. for the benchmark doc we should 1) add normalization step to replay harness, 2) report both raw replay and normalized-replay numbers, 3) capture kernel-switch counts and batch-size distribution.
jamie: wrote a small normalization shim: it coalesces adjacent prefill fragments if inter-token gap < 5ms and aligns to 512-token boundaries when possible. quick run: p95 delta narrows to 4%.
li: awesome. can you drop the shim into the replay harness and re-run the canonical run for the load plan? also add a test that flags >10% p95 discrepancy vs synthetic.
jamie: will do. plan: (a) add shim + tests, (b) instrument kernel-selection debug logs to capture preceding tokenization event id, (c) re-run 3 seeds and post results. starting now. ETA EOD.
sofia: also add a note in the benchmark methodology doc about prefill-dominant workloads and kernel hysteresis assumptions.
perf-bot: deploy-benchmark-agent: job 8893 queued by jamie at 1830567920
jamie: thanks. tagging @li @sofia for followups :eyes:
